nodes.title: Instructions
nodes.content:
How to use this board

Browse as a guest, unlock Student mode to contribute, or unlock Teacher mode to curate the board.

Every student contribution should finish with a first name, last initial and class in the author field.

After significant editing, a teacher should export a fresh class JSON file.

outcomes.text: Develops and evaluates questions and hypotheses for scientific investigation.
Designs and evaluates investigations to obtain primary and secondary data and information.
Conducts investigations to collect valid and reliable primary and secondary data and information.
Develops and evaluates the process of undertaking scientific investigations.

nodes.title: What initiates an investigation?
Investigate the observations, problems and unexpected findings that prompted recognised scientific investigations.
Explain why scientists pursued each investigation by identifying the data, relationships, prior conclusions or technological possibilities involved.
Determine the hypotheses tested in recognised scientific investigations.
Describe when investigators departed from a simple linear scientific method in order to test their hypotheses.
What type of methodology best suits a scientific investigation?
Evaluate the objectives and evidence collected in investigations by recognised scientists or scientific teams.
Justify the selected methodology in relation to the research subject and context.
Evaluate an investigation’s relevance by considering the peer-reviewed literature in its field.
Justify the suitability of the qualitative or quantitative data collected.
Develop and justify a method appropriate for testing a hypothesis arising from an observation.
How is the integrity of a scientific investigation judged?
Evaluate the investigation design by explaining the independent, dependent and controlled variables in relation to the research question.
Explain and evaluate sample selection and sample size.
Justify materials and equipment by considering relevance, availability, cost, risk and familiarity.
Assess ethical issues, including confidentiality, humane treatment and animal welfare.
Plan an achievable time frame and justify whether the investigation should be conducted individually or collaboratively.
Conduct the investigation and collect, record and analyse primary data.
Draw conclusions and propose further research by interpreting results and relating findings to the inquiry question and hypothesis.
Justify the methodology and any changes made to improve the evidence collected.
Describe potential beneficial and harmful consequences of applying the findings to a real-world context.
Evaluate validity by determining whether the investigation measured what it intended to measure.
Evaluate reliability through consistency, replication and measures used to reduce error.
What is the structure of an investigative report?
Review a published peer-reviewed report to identify conventions for reporting a practical investigation.
Identify the report’s purpose, error-reduction measures, language style, presentation and structure.
Compare the structure and function of the investigation process with the structure and function of its written report.
Prepare a scientific report for the student investigation.

outcomes.text: Develops and evaluates questions and hypotheses for scientific investigation.
Designs and evaluates investigations to obtain primary and secondary data and information.
Selects and processes appropriate qualitative and quantitative data and information using appropriate media.
Describes and explains how science drives the development of technologies.

nodes.title: How does technology enhance and/or limit scientific investigation?
Design an investigation that uses available technologies to measure independent and dependent variables and produce quantitative data.
Conduct the investigation, collect relevant data and evaluate the limitations of the technologies used.
Assess measuring devices for random error, systematic error and degree of accuracy.
Compare analogue and digital technologies for the accuracy of observations and measurements.
Assess the safety of selected technologies using safety data and Work Health and Safety guidance.
How have developments in technology led to advances in scientific theories and laws that, in turn, drive the need for further developments in technology?
Assess how technological developments have enabled evidence to accumulate for scientific theories, laws and models.
Assess how scientific theories, laws and models have driven the development of new technologies.

details: Refraction and reflection: microscopes and telescopes
Radioactive decay: radiotherapy and nuclear weapons

outcomes.text: Selects and processes appropriate qualitative and quantitative data and information using appropriate media.
Analyses and evaluates primary and secondary data and information.
Solves scientific problems using evidence, critical thinking and scientific processes.
Communicates scientific understanding for a specific audience or purpose.
Uses evidence-based analysis to support or refute a hypothesis.

nodes.title: How can a claim be tested?
Plan and conduct an investigation that tests a claim.
Evaluate the validity of the experimental design, reliability of the data and accuracy of the procedure.
Evaluate how sample selection and sample size affect investigation results.
Compare emotive advertising with evidence-based claims.
What factors can affect the way data can be interpreted, analysed and understood?
Justify the use of placebos, double-blind trials and control groups when drawing valid conclusions.
Evaluate societal and economic influences on the collection and interpretation of data.
What type of evidence is needed to draw valid conclusions?
Evaluate examples in which correlation has been misinterpreted as causation.

details: Hormone replacement therapy and coronary heart disease

nodes.title: How does the reporting of science influence the general public’s understanding of the subject?
Examine how a contemporary scientific debate is portrayed in mainstream media.
Evaluate how media use the terms theory, hypothesis, belief and law.
Compare a peer-reviewed journal article with a popular-media science article.
Analyse how conflicts of interest can suppress, distort or misrepresent scientific evidence and discuss safeguards.
Explain the halo effect and how positive perceptions can lead people to reject valid alternatives.
Analyse a pseudoscientific claim and the manipulation of scientific language or processes used to influence opinion.
Can the scientific community and process of peer review find ‘the truth’?
Research a scientist who falsified experimental results and explain how the fraud was uncovered.
Analyse the scientific debate around publication and the implications of ‘publish or perish’.
Evaluate whether science can effectively manage, review, replicate and validate the growing volume of published research.
Analyse how peer review contributes to the advancement and self-correction of science.
Discuss how fake or predatory science journals affect public perceptions of science.

Evaluates the implications of ethical, social, economic and political influences on science.

nodes.title: How do science-related events affect society’s view of science?
Investigate past science-related events and evaluate how they affected the public image of science.

nodes.title: Why is scientific research regulated?
Investigate why regulation is required in sensitive or high-risk areas of scientific research.

nodes.title: Investigate and assess ethical issues surrounding current scientific research and practice.
Investigate international scientific codes of conduct across contested areas of research and practice.
Evaluate the effectiveness of international regulation of scientific research and practice.
How do economic, social and political influences affect scientific research?
Evaluate the opportunity costs of space exploration compared with investment in major social needs.
Evaluate how scientific research contributes to economic development and human progress.
Evaluate the effects of scientific research, devices and applications on world health and human wellbeing.
Analyse how governments and large corporations influence the direction and funding of scientific research.
